mechanism_narrative: The ongoing decline in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES indicates fewer commuting trips, but the persistent week-to-week improvement in RETAIL_REC suggests local discretionary activity is still recovering. If this pattern continues, RETAIL_REC should be higher over the next four weeks than over the last four weeks.
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC stays below its prior-four-week mean despite continued stabilization or improvement in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES, this mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When RESIDENTIAL mobility remains elevated, households substitute away from outside shopping and recreation, keeping RETAIL_REC suppressed. Because RESIDENTIAL is still above baseline, the next four weeks should show a lower RETAIL_REC mean unless residential time falls back toward baseline.
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC rises above its last-four-week mean while RESIDENTIAL stays above baseline, the substitution mechanism is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: A fresh downward break in TRANSIT of more than 3 points week-on-week signals tightening movement restrictions or voluntary avoidance, which then reduces retail visits within one to two weeks. This predicts weaker RETAIL_REC unless transit stabilizes after the drop.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT is still near -46% and has been improving only gradually
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC does not decline within two weeks after a TRANSIT week-on-week drop exceeding 3 points, the threshold trigger is not operating.

mechanism_narrative: An improvement in PARKS mobility combined with a milder pullback in GROCERY_PHARM indicates more outdoor and neighborhood activity, which spills over into adjacent retail trips. The joint signal should raise RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC fails to improve when PARKS rises and GROCERY_PHARM remains near baseline or higher, the spillover mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES stabilizes around its current level while RESIDENTIAL continues to decline toward baseline, the time-budget tradeoff favors more discretionary out-of-home activity and retail visits. That balance should lift RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC does not rise while WORKPLACES holds steady and RESIDENTIAL falls toward baseline, the time-budget substitution claim is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: The recent acceleration in RETAIL_REC is driven by a lagged catch-up after earlier declines in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES begin to flatten. A continued flattening over the next week should translate into a modest further rise in retail mobility over a one-week horizon.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC improved from -20.1 to -13.3 across the snapshot
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC stalls or reverses within one week despite continued flattening in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES, the lagged catch-up mechanism fails.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous recovery in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES above their recent weekly means reflects looser access to jobs and destinations, which should feed through to retail and recreation with a short lag. The effect becomes visible within two weeks and is strongest when both series rise together.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both rise week-on-week
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC does not improve within two weeks after both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES rise week-on-week, the joint-access mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A rebound in PARKS mobility during warmer or more favorable outdoor conditions diverts trips into mixed leisure behavior and then supports retail visits in the following month. The mechanism predicts higher RETAIL_REC over four weeks, but only if PARKS continues above its recent trough rather than reverting.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises above its prior 2-week average by at least 5 points
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS moved from -21.9 to -10.9 in the latest week
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC does not exceed its last-four-week mean after PARKS rises at least 5 points above its prior two-week average, the outdoor-leisure spillover hypothesis is falsified.
